newsitem.title: USA: Residential Re notes rated triple-'A' by Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Residential Re notes rated triple-'A' by Fitch.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said it rated Residential Reinsurance Ltd's $163.8 million catastrophic risk based notes, class A-1, triple-'A'.
Residential Re's $313.2 million class A-2 notes were rated double-B, Fitch said.

Residential Re, a special purpose reinsurance company, issued the notes to provide USAA Group reinsurance for a single East Coast hurricane within a 12-month period generating losses losses in excess of $1 billion.

The ratings reflect Fitch's catastrophic risk based bond methodology, which incorporates a review and analysis of the ceding insurer's underlying book of business, the credit strength of the ceding insurer, the catastrophic event model, the resulting aggregate loss distribution, the structural soundness of the notes and the legal documentation supporting the transaction, Fitch said.
Residential Reinsurance and USAA hired Applied Insurance Research (AIR) to develop the catastrophic event model, which simulates hurricane occurrence and resulting loss.
The AIR model uses data from actual historical hurricane losses to generate thousands of hypothetical storms and the amount of damage resulting from each.
Upon review, Fitch said it requested the use of an alternative statistical method to better simulate the random nature of the data.

The risk capital provided by the notes, about 53 percent of the class A-1 and 100 percent of the class A-2, will be placed in a Regulation 114 trust, with Bankers Trust as trustee and invested in commercial paper, Fitch said..

The remaining $77 million proceeds from the class A-1 notes will be placed in a segregated collateral account which will be available to purchase U.S. Treasury strips with a minimum maturity value equal to the class A-1 principal.
Sufficiency of the funds to purchase these "defeasance securities" will be ensured through a contingency forward purchase agreement, Fitch said.

Chase Manhattan Bank will act as Indenture Trustee, interest rate swap agreements are with Merrill Lynch Capital Services, Inc. and the defeasance securities counterparty is Goldman Sachs Mitsui Marine Derivative Products, L.P.
The notes carry a one year base term, with a six-month extension at the option of USAA, which extends the term but not the risk coverage period.
Interest will be funded through premiums paid by USAA, interest earned on trust investments and any swap revenues.
In the absence of a loss occurrence, a hurricane resulting in losses over $1.0 billion, principal on both classes will be repaid at maturity.

In the event of a loss occurrence, partial or total interest and principal on the class A-2 notes will be forfeited and the related obligations of the issuer toward the class A-2 noteholders will be canceled.
Under the same scenario, interest on the class A-1 notes will discontinue and principal will be repaid upon maturity of the defeasance securities.
USAA is required to maintain a 20 percent risk of loss within the $500 million layer of risk in excess of the trigger amount.
